editorial_guidance.audience: People who love games; no technical background assumed.
editorial_guidance.rule: No game-design or development terminology in reader-facing text, headings, captions, contents, credits or metadata.
editorial_guidance.keep_internal: Build IDs, implementation status, technical art specifications and process notes belong in manifests and README only.
editorial_guidance.qualifications: Picture captions should describe the subject, action, atmosphere or useful player information. Do not discuss development history, earlier versions, prototype status or production progress. Keep asset provenance and development qualifications in internal records only. Remove tentative preview-artwork and exploring-an-idea captions. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable. Actual missing editorial content uses conspicuous TODOs.
editorial_guidance.preserve: Approved profiles and lore, spoiler-free policy and current names. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable.
editorial_guidance.writing_style: Follow AGENTS.md Writing Style: Avoid Formulaic AI Copy. Use natural, varied sentences and specific observations. Avoid repeated paired fragments, formulaic contrasts and generic trailer language. Review all creative copy for repetitive rhetorical patterns before publication.
editorial_guidance.corporate_horror: Imply the Spare Employee Dispenser's disturbing practices through corporate euphemisms and omissions. Do not disclose its lethal mechanism or describe bodily processing. Never refer to the viewer's screen or other fourth-wall-breaking presentation details in magazine copy.
editorial_guidance.pending_revision: Feedback through October 16 incorporated into edition 19; regeneration authorized.
editorial_guidance.todos: Actual unresolved editorial placeholders must say TODO: followed by the specific missing item. Use a conspicuous high-contrast box with bold type at least 18 pt, with sufficient space and no clipping. Never bury TODOs in small italic captions or replace them with vague caveats. Do not invent TODOs for existing artwork merely because gameplay is unfinished.
editorial_guidance.clogfather_revision: First description preserved; redundant paragraph and idle inset replaced with Tony horror reaction.

elements.text: DRAIN DAMAGE     /     SPECIAL CREATURE ISSUE     /     OCTOBER 2026
THE JOURNAL OF PLUMBING & CREATURE CONTAINMENT
Find out what has been making all that noise in the basement.
Tony and Sean take on the basement nobody wants to inspect.
THE CREW  02     •     CREATURE FEATURE  04     •     ACTION GALLERY  07
Tony is teaching Sean a trade that keeps getting stranger.

Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and keeping essential systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him off. A large spider might slow him down a little.

Plumbing runs in Tony's family. He brings that accumulated knowledge to the job, along with the patience to explain what he's doing. Sean has a great deal to learn, and Tony intends to give him the chance.
Tony's pressure gun fires quickly, so keep your aim steady and give yourself room when the creatures close in.

Sean wandered in looking for work and somehow ended up on Tony's crew. He's willing to help, although it's worth checking what he's holding before asking him to hand you a tool. Tony is showing him the ropes. There are quite a few ropes.
Sean arrived without much knowledge of plumbing. Tony took him on anyway. For now, enthusiasm is doing a lot of the work, and a patient teacher is keeping the rest moving.
Sean's heavy plunger launcher hits hard. Make each shot count, and leave yourself room while he reloads.

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing & Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it might be unpleasant.

BJ speaks calmly, keeps the jobs coming, and expects his employees to get on with them. If you're hoping the smiling face means he's concerned about your welfare, you may want to ask a more specific question.
BJ IS TAKING AN UNWELCOME INTEREST IN YOUR WORK.
COMPANY BENEFITS / THE SPARE EMPLOYEE DISPENSER

Mainframe Plumbing & Supply would like you to know that arrangements have been made. The Spare Employee Dispenser stands ready between service calls, its glass front offering a reassuring view of the company’s preparations. There is rust around the hinges and something familiar about the occupants. The accompanying leaflet describes them as reserve personnel. It asks employees to respect their rest and directs all further questions to the same leaflet.

The leaflet is particularly clear on continuity of service. Your assignments will remain on the schedule, your tools will still be required, and your name will stay on the rota. Several paragraphs explain how much the company values an experienced employee. The section headed “What this means for you” refers back to those paragraphs. We would have preferred a little more detail, but the cabinet does appear to be well stocked.
The company asks that reserve personnel not be disturbed.
A FIELD GUIDE TO A VERY BAD SERVICE CALL

This bad-tempered fixture has burning red eyes under a lid-like brow, ceramic teeth around its bowl, and short pipe legs. It patrols until a plumber gets too close, then closes the distance with a hop. The service appointment is unlikely to go as planned.
Service tip: Look for pipe legs, red eyes and teeth around the bowl. If it starts following you, the appointment has moved beyond routine maintenance.
THE HALO DOESN'T MAKE THE FANGS ANY LESS WORRYING.

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one sprouted wings and apparently started breeding. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed concerns about what this implies for heaven.
Tony: "I was hoping spiders went somewhere else when they died."
CREATURE FEATURE / THE BIG & THE BUZZING

A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have flushed. Wedged into the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the accumulated consequences back at anyone approaching.

The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.
This tight cloud of flies hurts plumbers and monsters alike when they cross its path.
LEAVE YOURSELF ROOM BEFORE THE FLUSHFIEND STARTS HOPPING.
A moving fixture is your cue to back away. By the time it reaches your boots, you will want more room than you left yourself.
FIELD TIP: Keep some clear floor behind you. A wall is a poor escape route.
DON'T LET IT CLOSE THE GAP.
DON'T LET IT CLOSE THE GAP.
The toilet follows Sean and hurts him when it catches him. After a hit, you have a brief chance to get clear before it can hurt you again. Use it.
Tony can keep the pressure on with quick shots. Sean needs a little more breathing room between heavy plungers. Either way, standing still gives the teeth time to catch up.
Watch the floor ahead as well as the creature behind. You need room for the next shot, the next landing and whatever the building has decided to do next.
Leave room for the hop before lining up another shot.
A CLOSER LOOK AT WHO'S CAUSING ALL THE TROUBLE.
Tony and Sean have rather different ideas about how much force a job needs.
From a bad-tempered fixture to an expensive pile of broken porcelain.
A halo offers very little reassurance when the fangs are this close.
The Septic Air Force keeps close company. Try not to join the formation.

Discharge Quarterly is a fictional journal for Drain Damage. The Plumbing, Heating & Creature Containment Association is fictional. No affiliation with Nintendo Power, GamePro or any real PHCC is implied. Pictures: Drain Damage art collection.
THAT IS WHY WE KEEP SPARES.
Please report for replacement. Your next service call is still waiting.
Check in as you are, then get back to work.

The Spare Employee Dispenser.
Your name is already on the schedule.

design_guidance.format: Eight-page 1990s magazine; grouped features, asymmetric columns, bright banners, bordered pictures, cutout characters and compact captions.
design_guidance.creatures: Four creatures share a two-page spread. One separate curated action gallery; no complete sheets.
design_guidance.references: User-supplied Nintendo Power / GamePro spreads; layouts reinterpreted with original game artwork.
